title: Incoming graphite can match Gaia20cdd infrared summaries without grain release after 2009 in a collisionless model
abstract: Persistent infrared light does not by itself give the date when dust grains formed. We test this for Gaia20cdd with directly lit graphite spheres and two published stellar models. Non-negative mixtures of 34 or 39 incoming paths match the 2010 WISE colour and 12 um summaries and the mean colour of 21 quiet NEOWISE visits in 2014-2024. All grains can leave bound parent orbits before 2010 with no added ejection speed. Each has radius 0.2957566 um. The selected masses are 1.52e23 or 6.79e22 g. The colour scores are close to a constant-colour reference, but the path weights are chosen to match that mean. This is a feasibility witness, not evidence for an incoming stream or a preferred source model. We also prove that a grain with constant radiation force ratio beta > 1 spends at most 1.183223 sqrt[R^3/((beta-1)GM)] inside radius R, for any initial velocity. Thus short warm residence and late arrival can coexist. The earlier circular-release timing result remains valid within its scope. Our witness does not fit optical dips, a full grain-size distribution, the later possible ice band, collisions or source dynamics. Code, path weights, model curves, checks, figures and exact external source hashes permit reproduction.

display.caption: A constructed incoming graphite ensemble matches the published infrared summaries. Later W3 is a model prediction. The paths are selected by design and do not establish the source.

Repelled grains have a finite warm residence, yet grains released before 2010 can reach closest approach at different later dates. The bound assumes constant beta greater than one and no other forces.
